name: mongosh
description: Connect to a MongoDB deployment with the MongoDB Shell.

flags.description: Password; omit the value to be prompted
Database the user was created in (often admin)

examples.description: Connect to mongodb://localhost:27017
Connect and select the myapp database
Connect to an Atlas cluster via SRV record (prompts for password)
Connect with explicit options and authenticate against admin

notes: mongosh replaced the legacy mongo shell, which was removed in MongoDB 6.0.
Quote connection strings in the shell, and URL-encode special characters (@ : / ? # [ ]) in passwords.
Don't put real passwords in the URI on shared machines; omit the password and let mongosh prompt.

name: mongosh --eval
description: Run a JavaScript expression or script file non-interactively.

flags.description: Print the --eval result as Extended JSON

examples.description: Print a value and exit
Execute a script file against myapp
Health check suitable for scripts

notes: Since mongosh 2.2, non-interactive runs (--eval, --file) are quiet by default; add --no-quiet to see the banner

name: show dbs
description: List databases on the server along with their size on disk.

examples.description: List all databases
Programmatic equivalent returning only names

notes: A database only appears after it contains at least one document or collection.

name: use
description: Switch to a database (it is created lazily on first write).

examples.description: Switch to the myapp database
Print the current database name
Query another database without switching

name: show collections
description: List collections in the current database.

examples.description: List collection names
Return collection names as an array
Explicitly create a 10 MB capped collection

name: db.stats()
description: Show storage statistics for the current database.

examples.description: Collections, objects, data size and index size
Report sizes in megabytes

name: db.dropDatabase()
description: Drop the current database or a single collection.

examples.description: Drop the myapp_test database
Drop just the sessions collection and its indexes

notes: WARNING: data and indexes are deleted immediately with no confirmation. Always check the output of db first.
Back up with mongodump before dropping anything in production.

name: $jsonSchema validator
description: Enforce document structure on a collection with JSON Schema validation

examples.command: db.createCollection("users", { validator: { $jsonSchema: { bsonType: "object", required: ["email", "createdAt"], properties: { email: { bsonType: "string" }, createdAt: { bsonType: "date" } } } } })
examples.description: Create a collection that rejects documents missing email or createdAt

examples.command: db.runCommand({ collMod: "users", validator: { $jsonSchema: { bsonType: "object", required: ["email"] } }, validationLevel: "moderate", validationAction: "warn" })
examples.description: Add validation to an existing collection, logging violations instead of rejecting
Show the current validator

notes: validationLevel: strict (default) checks all inserts and updates; moderate skips updates to documents that were already invalid
validationAction: error (default) rejects invalid writes; warn allows them and logs a warning
Existing documents aren't checked when you add a validator; query with { $nor: [ { $jsonSchema: ... } ] } to find violators

name: db.collection.find()
description: Query documents with a filter, projection, sort and limit.

examples.description: Find all active users
Filter with an operator and return only selected fields
Latest 10 orders in a set of statuses
Match with a regular expression

notes: Common operators: $eq, $ne, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $in, $nin, $exists, $regex, $and, $or.
mongosh shows 20 results at a time; type it to iterate further.

name: db.collection.findOne()
description: Return the first document matching a filter, or null.

examples.description: Look up a user by email
Look up a document by _id

name: db.collection.insertOne()
description: Insert one or many documents into a collection.

examples.command: db.users.insertOne({ name: "Ada", email: "ada@example.com", createdAt: new Date() })
examples.description: Insert a single document
Insert several documents at once
Continue inserting remaining docs if one fails (e.g. duplicate key)

notes: Collections are created automatically on first insert.
An _id ObjectId is generated if you don't provide one.

name: db.collection.updateOne()
description: Modify matching documents using update operators.

examples.description: Set a field on the first match
Update every matching document
Increment a counter and append to an array
Insert the document if no match exists

notes: Common operators: $set, $unset, $inc, $push, $addToSet, $pull, $rename.
updateMany({}, ...) updates every document in the collection; double-check the filter.
Use replaceOne() to replace a whole document instead of modifying fields.

name: db.collection.deleteOne()
description: Delete one or many documents matching a filter.

examples.description: Delete a single document
Delete all documents older than a date

notes: WARNING: deleteMany({}) removes every document in the collection. Run the same filter with countDocuments() first.
To expire documents automatically, use a TTL index instead of scheduled deletes.

name: db.collection.findOneAndUpdate()
description: Atomically update one document and return it (before or after the change)

examples.description: Atomic sequence generator: returns the incremented value

examples.command: db.jobs.findOneAndUpdate({ status: "queued" }, { $set: { status: "running", startedAt: new Date() } }, { sort: { priority: -1, createdAt: 1 }, returnDocument: "after" })
examples.description: Claim the highest-priority queued job
Delete a document and return what was deleted
Replace a whole document and return the original

notes: Returns the original document by default; pass returnDocument: "after" (or returnNewDocument: true) for the updated one
sort decides which document is modified when several match
With upsert: true, put a unique index on the filter fields to avoid duplicate inserts under concurrency

name: db.collection.countDocuments()
description: Count documents matching a filter.

examples.description: Exact count of matching documents
Fast approximate total from collection metadata
List the distinct values of a field

notes: count() and cursor.count() are deprecated; use countDocuments() or estimatedDocumentCount().

name: db.collection.aggregate()
description: Run an aggregation pipeline to filter, group, join and reshape data.

examples.description: Top 5 customers by total paid
Join each order with its user
Count events per day

notes: Put $match and $sort early so the pipeline can use indexes.
Stages are limited to 100 MB of RAM unless you pass { allowDiskUse: true } (default true from MongoDB 6.0).
MongoDB 9.0 also caps memory per operation (by default the greater of 1 GB or 20% of RAM); exceeding it fails with ExceededMemoryLimit

name: db.collection.createIndex()
description: Create an index to speed up queries or enforce uniqueness.

examples.description: Unique ascending index on email
Compound index for filtering by customer and sorting by date
TTL index that deletes sessions after one hour
Text index for $text search

notes: Order matters in compound indexes: follow the Equality, Sort, Range rule.
Index builds on large collections consume resources; schedule them off-peak.

name: db.collection.getIndexes()
description: List the indexes on a collection.

examples.description: Show index definitions and names
Show how often each index has been used

name: db.collection.dropIndex()
description: Remove an index from a collection.

examples.description: Drop an index by name
Drop an index by key pattern

notes: Dropping an index used by queries can make them dramatically slower. Consider db.collection.hideIndex() first to test the impact.

name: cursor.explain()
description: Show the query plan and execution statistics for a query.

examples.description: Check docs examined vs returned and which index was used
Explain an aggregation pipeline

notes: COLLSCAN in the winning plan means a full collection scan; IXSCAN means an index was used.
Compare totalDocsExamined with nReturned to spot inefficient queries.

name: db.createUser()
description: Create a database user with roles.

examples.command:
use admin
db.createUser({ user: "app_user", pwd: passwordPrompt(), roles: [{ role: "readWrite", db: "myapp" }] })
examples.description: Create an app user with read/write on myapp (prompts for password)
Create a superuser in the admin database
List users in the current database
Add a role to an existing user

notes: Users belong to the database they are created in; clients must authenticate against it (--authenticationDatabase).
passwordPrompt() avoids leaving the password in shell history.

name: db.currentOp()
description: Show in-progress operations and kill long-running ones.

examples.description: Show operations running longer than 5 seconds
Terminate an operation by its opid
Show current and available connection counts
Aggregation-stage equivalent that can be filtered and projected further

name: db.setProfilingLevel()
description: Record slow operations in the database profiler to find queries that need indexes

examples.description: Profile operations slower than 100 ms in the current database
Only profile queries slower than 2 seconds
Show the 5 most recent profiled operations
Show the current level and threshold
Turn the profiler off

notes: Level 0 = off, 1 = slow ops only, 2 = everything (expensive; avoid in production)
Since MongoDB 8.0, slowness is measured by workingMillis, which excludes time spent waiting for locks and flow control
Settings reset on restart; set operationProfiling.mode in mongod.conf to persist them
Not available on mongos or Atlas M0/Flex clusters

name: setFeatureCompatibilityVersion
description: Check or set the feature compatibility version (FCV), the last step of a major-version upgrade

examples.description: Show the current FCV
Enable 9.0 features after every member runs 9.0 binaries

examples.command: db.adminCommand({ setFeatureCompatibilityVersion: "9.0", confirm: true, dryRun: true })
examples.description: Check for incompatible data without changing anything (8.3+)

notes: Upgrade binaries one major version at a time, then raise the FCV; a lower FCV keeps the option to downgrade binaries
confirm: true is required (MongoDB 7.0+)
WARNING: once new-version features are used, downgrading the FCV can fail with CannotDowngrade; wait through a burn-in period before raising it
Run on the primary or on mongos; getParameter doesn't work through mongos

name: mongostat / mongotop
description: Live per-second server stats (mongostat) and per-collection read/write time (mongotop)

flags.description: Report every member of a replica set or every shard via mongos

examples.description: Inserts, queries, updates, cache usage and connections every second
10 rows, averaged over 5-second intervals
Watch every replica set member at once
Time spent reading and writing each collection, every 5 seconds

notes: Part of the MongoDB Database Tools, installed separately from the server and mongosh; run from the OS shell, not mongosh
Avoid passwords on the command line; let the tool prompt or use --config with a YAML file

name: mongodump
description: Create a binary (BSON) backup of a database or deployment.

flags.description: Write a single archive file (or stdout) instead of a directory
Only dump documents matching a JSON filter
Capture a point-in-time snapshot on replica sets

examples.description: Dump every database to ./backup
Dump one database to a single compressed archive
Dump a single collection from Atlas

notes: Part of the MongoDB Database Tools, installed separately from the server and mongosh.
For large production clusters prefer filesystem snapshots or Atlas backups; mongodump can be slow and impacts performance.

name: mongorestore
description: Restore data from a mongodump backup.

flags.description: Drop each collection before restoring it

examples.description: Restore everything from a dump directory
Restore from a compressed archive, replacing existing collections
Restore only one collection
Restore into a differently named database

notes: WARNING: --drop deletes existing collections in the target before restoring
Without --drop, documents with an existing _id are skipped, not overwritten.
Prefer --nsInclude over the deprecated --db/--collection options.

name: mongoexport
description: Export a collection to JSON or CSV.

examples.description: Export to newline-delimited JSON
Export selected fields to CSV
Export filtered documents as a JSON array

notes: Not a backup tool: JSON/CSV loses some BSON type fidelity. Use mongodump for backups.

name: mongoimport
description: Import JSON, CSV or TSV data into a collection.

flags.description: Input is a single JSON array
Use the first CSV/TSV line as field names

examples.description: Import newline-delimited JSON
Import CSV using the first row as field names
Upsert a JSON array matched on sku

notes: WARNING: --drop deletes the existing collection first

name: rs.status()
description: Show the health and state of each replica set member.

examples.description: Show member states (PRIMARY, SECONDARY), health and optime

examples.command: rs.status().members.map(m => ({ name: m.name, state: m.stateStr, health: m.health }))
examples.description: Compact summary of members
Show whether this node is primary and list the set's hosts
Show replication lag for each secondary

notes: db.hello() replaces the deprecated isMaster command.

name: rs.initiate()
description: Initialize and manage a replica set.

examples.description: Initialize a three-member replica set
Show the current replica set configuration
Add a member
Ask the primary to step down and trigger an election

notes: Each mongod must be started with the same --replSet name before rs.initiate().
rs.stepDown() causes a brief window with no primary; writes will fail until a new one is elected.

name: db.collection.watch()
description: Open a change stream to react to inserts, updates and deletes in real time

examples.command:
const cs = db.orders.watch([{ $match: { operationType: "insert" } }])
while (!cs.isClosed()) { if (cs.hasNext()) printjson(cs.next()) }
examples.description: Print new orders as they are inserted
Include the current full document with update events
Watch every collection in the current database

notes: Requires a replica set or sharded cluster (a single-node replica set works for development)
Store each event's _id (resume token) and pass it as resumeAfter/startAfter to continue after a restart; mongosh doesn't auto-resume
For pre-change documents, enable changeStreamPreAndPostImages on the collection and use fullDocumentBeforeChange
